name: Eileen Bloom
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember tearing up a job application that mentioned the ridge.” Tuesday often includes a stop at Breakwater Way, where Eileen stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I passed my test and kept turning down jobs east of the ridge. Nobody knew the real reason.
appearance: Eileen is easy to recognize by a loose dark braid and a small notch in the left eyebrow. Usually dressed in a red windbreaker with a replacement button a shade darker than the others, Eileen gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in when listening.
personality: Eileen gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. Eileen privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To reach the far side at a pace the learner chooses.
family: Kate Dinh is Eileen’s older cousin. A family picnic once turned into a six-hour wait at a bus shelter. What they remember best is the oldest relative teaching everyone to keep score with gravel. Eileen is very good company when everybody is stranded. Asked about *The fountain score*, Kate says, “I typed the program on my late partner's machine and got cast as its percussionist.”
connections: David Soto (parent). A parent has to let the learner speak first about what happened on the ridge.

reactions.situation: The learner turns back before the crest
reactions.response: Eileen treats turning back as a completed decision and finds somewhere calm to stop.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Eileen offers the worker something dry first and leaves it to them whether to pursue the apology.
